## System Overview:

# Joint Controller (Repeater)

- **Overview:**  
  - This node updates motors with desired state. The main loop on this thread would essentially take whatever the most recent velocity control value that has been written in the UUID\_to\_power\_value map and send it over can to each motor. This loop should be running at a 333 ms loop (or faster) adding a series of packets to all motors connected.  
  - This node should essentially loop over all motor entries every 333 ms and check if they need to have the motor controller state updated (only if the power setting is \> 0). Otherwise if a motor power value is 0 don’t send anything to avoid clogging the CAN line.  
  - The node will receive data via the subscribed topics from Mission Control Bridge or Controller Tester  
- **State**  
  - UUID\_to\_power\_ratio  
    - Map of motor to multiplier that is applied to each of the   
  - UUID\_to\_power\_value  
    - Map of motor CAN UUID to the actual motor power  
    - The power value is only updated upon startup and whenever a user interface request comes in to set the value (ie Mission Control Bridge Node or Controller Node)  
- **Publishers**  
  - “/can\_tx”   
    - Description  
      - This publisher publishes the can packet to the desired motor to update the velocity. This publisher should essentially be a callback that checks what motor is desired based on the subscribed topic then calls the correct motor can packet builder and sends the can packet by publishing to the node.  
- **Subscribers**  
  - Note:   
    - Some of these will be temporary for SAR or intended for use for SAR/ debugging. For example handling motor requests directly through the mission control bridge might be disabled or have its own state to determine whether setting the motor power of individual motors is allowed.   
      - Having a “motor set” mode is important as we don’t want accidental misclicks from mission control messing with control loops for whatever reason  
  - **“**/mc/drive\_request**”**  
    - Type:   
      - Vector2  
        - \[0\] power  
        - \[1\] drive  
    - Description  
      - Every time the callback for this topic is triggered, this specific callback handler will convert the power value in the zeroth index \-1 \< theta \< 1 range to a power value. This power value is then scaled based on the UUID\_to\_power\_ratio and then placed in the right index for UUID\_to\_power\_value.  
      - Since a drive request requires controlling multiple motors, the code here will have to hardcode the UUID of what motors to set. In this case it would be forward angular velocity for all four drive motors as well as orienting the back two swerve modules to face forward.  
        - Keep in mind that the swerve module is positional and thus requires setting the position as opposed to setting the power value.  
      - Received from either mission control bridge node or controller node.  
  - “mc/\<joint field\>\_power”  
    - Type:  
      - Double  
        - Power Value  
    - Description  
      - The callback for this function updates the UUID\_to\_power\_value mapping. This will allow the value within UUID\_to\_power\_value to send the power value to the correct motor in the next joint repeater task. Like the above drive request, each motor power request gets scaled by the specific UUID power ratio value.  
      - Joints are generally an abstraction for a single degree of freedom thus occasionally requiring the orchestration of multiple or multiple motors. This means that a joint power request might require setting the velocity on multiple motor UUID’s to achieve whatever movement that you want.  
      - There is some hardware that are defined as joints however are not joints being laser, lights and hand actuator. These require a single can packet get sent to toggle them or turn them on. The call back for these must not update the power mapping and instead just dispatch the respective can packet.  
  - “cn/\<motor field\>\_power”  
    - Double  
      - Power Value  
    - Description  
      - This callback handles setting the motor values directly. Very similarly to the joint power setting, we do a translation with the UUID power ratio mapping and then set the correct power in the power value map. This function should be relatively simple, only requiring doing a bunch of map lookups and not needing to orchestrate any motors  
    - Notes  
      - Might need to include some fault handling thus to not destroy any differential joints

# Mission Control Bridge

- **State**  
  - Camera\_Frame  
    - String  
      - Base 64 encoded camera frame. The code should store the state for the camera as a base 64 so that as soon as mission control requests the camera frame we can respond with the least compute overhead.  
- **Json Packets handled**  
  - Emergency stop request  
    - Json String Type: “emergencyStopRequest”  
    - Handling  
      - Invoke the “e\_stop” action.  
      - Most likely the main rover server has not been established yet. This will trigger a kill power to all motors and any other safety fall backs we may install. Ensure that a message is printed out for this.  
  - Operation mode request  
    - Json String Type: “operationModeRequest”  
    - Handling  
      - Publish to “/mc/operation\_mode” topic with the string that is in the mode field of the json packet  
  - Enable Motors Request  
    - Json String Type: “enableMotorsRequest”  
    - Handling:  
      - Send action related to enabling the motors. If action server is not setup at this point just replace with a debug log and warning.  
  - Drive Request  
    - Json String Type: “driveRequest”  
    - Handling  
      - Publish to “mc/drive\_request” with the fields in the packet  
  - Joint Power Request  
    - Json String Type: “jointPowerRequest”  
    - Handling  
      - Parses the json packet to get the joint in the “joint" field  
      - The double value in the power field will then be sent to the topic with the name “mc/\<joint field\>\_power”. The possible joint field as of 11/14/26 are shown below in Figure 1\. For example the topic for arm base would be “mc/armBase\_power”  
  - Joint Position Request  
    - Json String Type: “jointPositionRequest”  
    - Handling:  
      - Same as the power request, fetch the joint field from the packet labeled “joint”  
      - Then the double value that is in the “power” field gets sent on the topic labeled as the following “mc/\<joint field\>\_position”. The power field will be published as a double.  
    - Notes:  
      	We are going to have this feature this year\! Woo\!

- **Actions**  
  - “e\_stop” \-\> action  
    -  Send out terminate motor speed to all motors as well as e stop packets. Hardcode internal state of the motor control node to prevent any publishing of can topics.  
  - “enable\_motors”  
- **Publishers**  
  -   
  - “/mc/drive\_request”  
    - Type:   
      - Vector 3  
    - Description:  
      - First index is how much power going forward range \-1 to 1  
      - Second index is rotate left or right \-1 to 1	  
      - The third index is unused.  
      - This topic will be read by the drive node where it will decide will perform the controls of setting the front two motors and the   
    - Notes:  
      - Although we discussed that this node will output the desired vector of the robot, I think it makes more sense if the power is just how fast we spin the wheels and the rotation is just the rotation. We would simply just scale the \-1 \< theta \< 1 range to \- 90 \< theta \< 90\.  
  - “/mc/operation\_mode”  
    - Type:  
      - String  
    - Description  
      - Mode of rover. This determines whether it is teleoperated or autonomous  
      - Can be either “autonomous”  
  - “/mc/append\_waypoint”  
    - Type  
      - Waypoint  
        - Float: latitude  
        - Float: longitude  
        - Bool: isApporximate  
        - Bool: isGate   
    - Description  
      - This is the next waypoint that the rover will go to in the series of points that it has. The autonomy node is responsible for handling and keeping track of all the waypoints and ensuring that it goes to the correct location in order.  
    - Notes  
      - There should be a way to see if this fails. It might be good to make this an action, however I don’t know how we can include state with actions so topics make the most sense for the time being.  
  - “/mc/\<joint field\>\_power”  
    - Type  
      - Double  
    - Description  
      - This topic calls the function to essentially update the power of a specific motor. This topic will just produce the raw mission control \-1 \< theta \< 1 rotation value and send it over to the Joint controller repeater. This will be the most basic form of control that we will have where we have essentially no control loops running and just setting raw power values.

# Controller Node

- **Publishers:**  
  - **“**/mc/drive\_request**”**  
    - Type:   
      - Vector2  
        - \[0\] power  
        - \[1\] drive  
    - Description  
      - Based on the WASD inputs on the keyboard send a power value correlated to how much power to give to the motors. The power value should be the same no matter what since driving in any direction will result in the standard move forward power value (scale this to whatever is easiest for control)  
      - The drive direction will need to be computed based on the combination of WASD keys imputed. If the operator wants a 45 degree rotation of the wheel by pressing WA or WD then send that in the drive field.  
      - To correctly emulate the mission control behavior as the drive value is intended to be between \-1 and 1 where \-1 is requesting the wheels turn left at max power and 1 is requesting wheels turn right at max power, convert the desired angle to a range of \-1 to 1 to fit the drive value.  
  - “mc/\<joint field\>\_power”  
    - Double  
      - Power Value  
    - Description  
      - Send the power value of whatever joint. These joints are defined in the previously pasted name\_to\_jointid mapping.  
  - “cn/\<motor field\>\_po\\wer”  
    - Double  
      - Power Value  
    - Description  
      - Send the power value to specific motors. This topic will primarily act for debugging to ensure that we are able to set the value of specific motors without dealing with the “joint” abstraction. On the other end the motor field gets directly translated into a motor UUID and the power gets set based on the double value in the power value field.  
    - Notes:  
      - Motor naming for \<motor field\>:  
        -  frontTireLeft,  
        -   frontTireRight,  
        -   rearTireLeft,  
        -   rearTireRight,  
        -   armBase,  
        -   shoulder,  
        -   elbow,  
        -   forearm,  
        -   wristDiffRight,  
        -   wristDiffLeft,  
        -   telemetry,  
        -   hand,

# Drive Node

- **State**  
  - Drive Type:  
    - Enum  
      - Init  
      - Crab  
      - Car  
      - Rotate  
    - Description  
      - Within the drive node, we will have a state machine that determines what kind of driving behavior to expect.  
      - Each of the following state transitions will block all requests on state transitions to avoid messing with wheels when in intermediate states. This means that the wheels must orient themselves to original position   
      - In all modes but Car, all swerve motors are in a fixed position. However in car mode the front two swerve motors are able to rotate with 180 degrees of freedom (-90\<=Θ\<=90) where 0 is facing forward.
